rule: Scheduler registry is external authority. Worker loops must never mutate scheduler state. Any observed enabled-state, ID, minute, timezone, or task-count drift is an incident and must be repaired by the orchestrator, not by a worker run.
mutable_state_rule: finalization_state, heartbeat, and evidence_state are monotonic by RUN_ID; delayed older invocations are SUPERSEDED.
scheduler_mutation_rule: Workers must never invoke scheduler/task-management tools. Only the external orchestrator may repair enabled-state or schedule drift.

orchestrator_mutation_guard.rule: Before any automations.update on one of the restored five, read the live registry. Do not mutate a task whose last_run_time is within the current invocation window, and do not mutate during the protected pre-slot window.
orchestrator_mutation_guard.rationale: Prompt/config changes during an active scheduler invocation can contaminate or interrupt the slot and invalidate it as natural protocol evidence.
